book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: Casual son, Dickens character losing it

indicators.note: the character's name is losing something, so those letters drop away from it

parts.note: Bob Cratchit, Scrooge's put-upon clerk in A Christmas Carol
taken as written: the two letters to drop

explanation.surface: A laid-back lad is likened to a Dickens figure who has lost his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing it' reads as an idiom for losing one's temper, but here it means the letters IT go from the end of CRATCHIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratch team or scratch meal is thrown together informally, without preparation, so the word works as an adjective for something casual.

clue.text: GER ONO DW Ne Silver brought in set aside — it's knocked horribly

indicators.note: the metal is brought into the middle of the other word

parts.note: money set aside has been saved

explanation.surface: Silver put into the savings box gets dented and bashed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be savaged is to be attacked viciously or criticised brutally, which is being knocked about cruelly.

clue.text: Wander from country house that's lost its roof

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof is the top letter, and it has gone

parts.note: a grange is a country house with farm buildings

explanation.surface: Someone drifts away from a ruined manor with no roof.
explanation.definitionFit: To range is to roam freely over an area, so it is a synonym for wander.

clue.text: Runs of cards not including ace

indicators.note: the cards are counted without the single card named

parts.note: tarots are the cards used for fortune-telling

explanation.surface: A sequence of playing cards without the ace in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like card sequences, but it is the definition: the trots is slang for diarrhoea.
explanation.definitionFit: The trots and the runs are both informal names for diarrhoea.

clue.text: One who has little bird beheaded — get angry about that

indicators.note: the anger goes round the headless bird

parts.note: to get hot under the collar

indicators.note: with the head cut off, the first letter goes

parts.note: a raven is a large black bird

explanation.surface: A man who has decapitated a small bird makes another man furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little bird' looks like one phrase, but 'little' finishes the definition and the bird is a big one.
explanation.definitionFit: The have-nots are the poor, people who possess very little, as opposed to the haves.

clue.text: Superintended child's broadcast

parts.note: ch. is the dictionary abbreviation for child; the 's stands for 'is', joining it to what follows
a programme that is broadcast has been aired

explanation.surface: Someone oversaw a children's radio or television programme going out.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'child's' as 'child is': the abbreviation CH followed by AIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a meeting or committee is to preside over it, so a person who chaired something superintended it.

clue.text: Warden's list put up with despicable person at the top

indicators.note: the cur goes above the list, first in the down answer

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties

explanation.surface: A warden's duty roster is posted with a nasty character named first.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator is the keeper of a museum or collection, a warden in the old sense of guardian.

clue.text: Like the arrangement of some flowers in a batch with others

definitions.text: Like the arrangement of some flowers

parts.note: taken as written
a crop is a batch of produce, or students, gathered at one time
et al, Latin et alii, and others

explanation.surface: Some flowers are arranged in a vase together with a mixed bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Acropetal is a botanical term, so the plain pieces carry the weight.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany, acropetal describes flowers or leaves maturing in succession from the base of the stem toward the tip.

clue.text: Teacher's office or class containing a black container for rubbish

indicators.note: the class holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: rate means class, as in first-rate
taken as written
a bin holds rubbish

explanation.surface: A school staffroom or classroom with a black rubbish bin in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teacher' sounds like a schoolteacher, but the teacher is a rabbi, a Jewish religious teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbinate is the post or office of a rabbi, whose title means my master or teacher.

clue.text: Hesitant little girl meeting the heartless boy

parts.note: Di is a short form of Diana
taken as written

indicators.note: with its heart gone, the middle letter drops out

parts.note: Roy, a boy's name

explanation.surface: A shy girl meets a cold-hearted young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' attaches to the boy, not 'the': only ROY loses its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dithery keeps wavering and cannot decide, which is to be indecisive.

clue.text: City University probes vehicle insurance

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle

indicators.note: something that probes pokes inside, so this letter goes into the other pieces

parts.note: an insurance policy gives cover

explanation.surface: A city university researches motor insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle insurance' looks like one phrase, but it is two pieces side by side, and the opening 'City' is the definition, not part of a university's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Vancouver is a large port city in British Columbia, on Canada's Pacific coast.

clue.text: Artist coming to club in the capital

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
a bat is a club for hitting a ball

explanation.surface: A painter arrives at a nightclub somewhere in the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The capital' sounds like London, but it is a capital elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the seat of government of Morocco, a coastal city on the Atlantic.

clue.text: Like seaweed covering island's rock

indicators.note: one piece covers the other, wrapping round it

parts.note: most seaweed is green
I for island plus the 's gives the two letters

explanation.surface: Seaweed has grown over the stone of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Greisen is an obscure geological term, so the wordplay has to carry it.
explanation.definitionFit: Greisen is a granite rock altered by hot gases into a mix of quartz and mica.

clue.text: Joint winner of team competition?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lean joint of beef cut from the upper leg
second meaning, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split of the cut of beef into TOP and SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchers sell topside as a roasting cut, while a top side is the leading team in a contest.

clue.text: Sailor hugged by Greek goddess — one can sense the radiation given off

definitions.text: one can sense the radiation given off

indicators.note: the goddess wraps her arms round the sailor, so he sits inside her name

parts.note: Demeter is the Greek goddess of the harvest
OS, an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A goddess embraces a sailor, and you can feel the heat coming off them.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual spelling is dosimeter, but dosemeter is an accepted variant and is the one the wordplay gives.
explanation.definitionFit: A dosemeter is a badge or instrument worn to measure the dose of ionizing rays a person has absorbed.

clue.text: Idler does need to be beaten (shirked)

indicators.note: letters that are beaten are knocked into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: A lazy person deserves a thrashing for dodging his duty.
explanation.walkthrough: To soldier, in older slang, is to shirk work while making a show of doing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiering in this sense is malingering, so to have soldiered is to have avoided work.

clue.text: Reformed prostitute made angel dance

indicators.note: the letters are made to dance into a different order

parts.note: taken as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: A fallen woman who has turned good is made an angel and dances.
explanation.definitionFit: A magdalene, after Mary Magdalene of the Gospels, is a penitent woman who has given up a life on the streets.

clue.text: Model interrupted by commercial flunkey

indicators.note: the advert breaks into the middle of the model

parts.note: a model car or train is a toy
a commercial is an advert, an ad

explanation.surface: A fashion model is cut short by an advert break, or by a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady is a fawning hanger-on, just as a flunkey is a servile underling.

clue.text: Prison authority little good to superior inmate

parts.note: G is the short form of good
U is upper-class, the superior social register
an old lag is a long-serving convict

explanation.surface: A prison governor shows a little kindness to a privileged prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG is British slang for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Gulag was the Soviet agency that ran the labour camps, and the name came to mean the camp system itself.

clue.text: Heroine in play said to be a chatterbox

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the surname gives the answer's sound

parts.note: Hedda Gabler, the title role of Ibsen's play

explanation.surface: A theatre's leading lady is reputed to talk nonstop.
explanation.definitionFit: A gabbler talks rapidly and endlessly, which is what a chatterbox does.

clue.text: Director bothered about new role

indicators.note: the first word goes round the second, enclosing it

parts.note: if you cared about something it bothered you

indicators.note: a new version of the word role has its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: A film director is upset about a fresh part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Director' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the definition: the answer is a particular director.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Carol Reed was the British film-maker behind The Third Man and Oliver!

clue.text: Fusses about movable Easter

parts.note: c., circa, is Latin for about

indicators.note: Easter is a movable feast; here the letters move about

parts.note: taken as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: People get worked up because Easter falls on a different date each year.
explanation.walkthrough: Easter really is a movable feast, which disguises 'movable' as plain description.
explanation.definitionFit: To create, in British colloquial use, is to make a fuss or complain loudly.

clue.text: Boasting leader avoided ridicule

indicators.note: the leading letter is left out

parts.note: bragging is boasting

explanation.surface: A bragging chief steered clear of mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragging is teasing or mocking someone, a noun close in sense to ridicule.

clue.text: Fault of top lady with 'Resign! going round

indicators.note: the resignation goes round the Queen, enclosing her

parts.note: to demit office is an old-fashioned way to resign it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A grand lady is blamed while people shout at her to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for the monarch, the top lady in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A demerit is a black mark or failing, so it means a fault or shortcoming.

clue.text: Army unit ordered to collect equipment

indicators.note: the order gathers the gear up inside it

parts.note: bade is the old past tense of bid, to command
rig is a set of gear or apparatus

explanation.surface: A detachment of soldiers is told to go and fetch kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is a large military formation made up of several battalions.

clue.text: General manager entertaining golf club's old woman

indicators.note: the manager entertains the club as a guest, holding it inside

parts.note: the R and A, the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews, governs golf

explanation.surface: A company boss hosts the wife of a golf club member.
explanation.walkthrough: The R&A is golf's ruling club in Scotland; spelt out, it gives three letters for the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandam is an archaic word for a grandmother, and so for any elderly female.

clue.text: An attempt to restrict gross belligerence from yobs

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the attempt restricts the other letters, closing round them

parts.note: a go is a try

explanation.surface: An effort is made to curb the gross aggression of hooligans.
explanation.walkthrough: Gr is a standard abbreviation for gross, the measure of twelve dozen.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggressive, violent behaviour of the sort louts go in for.

clue.text: Piece of info from union held in check

indicators.note: the union is held inside the dam

parts.note: a dam checks a river's flow
TU, a trade union

explanation.surface: A snippet of information from a trade union is kept back.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single fact or item of data, the singular of data.

clue.text: Considerable cellar gentleman keeps

indicators.note: the phrase keeps the answer inside it, across the two words

parts.note: the words that hold the answer

explanation.surface: A gentleman keeps a sizeable wine cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: Large and considerable both describe something of great size or amount.

clue.text: Reported story, spat on account of inconsiderate driver

indicators.note: said out loud, the two words give the answer's sound

parts.note: a tale is a story
a spat is a short cloth gaiter worn over the shoe

explanation.surface: A newspaper story says a road row broke out because of a selfish motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spat' reads as a quarrel, but it is the Edwardian garment covering the ankle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailgater drives too close behind another car, a classic bit of thoughtless motoring.

clue.text: Army branch's uniform must be correct

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a branch of the British Army
dress is formal uniform, as in mess dress

explanation.surface: A regiment insists its uniform be worn properly.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress a wrong or an imbalance is to put it right, so the verb means set right.

clue.text: Man at wedding losing ring settled for washer

indicators.note: the groom loses one of his letters

parts.note: the groom is the man getting married
O is ring-shaped
to meet a bill is to settle it

explanation.surface: A bridegroom who has dropped the wedding ring paid for a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' tempts as the wedding band and 'washer' as someone who washes; both are mechanical.
explanation.definitionFit: A grommet is a ring of metal or rubber that lines a hole, the same job as a washer.
